title: Can AI tame a ‘Godzilla’ El Niño?
source_used: Gizmodo (related coverage of the El Nino itself); the Financial Times article could not be opened (consent/paywall page)
key_facts: [Financial Times headline only] The FT asks "Can AI tame a Godzilla El Nino?" in a piece published 17 Oct 2026.
[Gizmodo, 16 Oct 2026] Gizmodo describes the 2026-27 El Nino as the strongest on record and still intensifying.
[Gizmodo] NOAA released its seasonal outlook on 15 Oct 2026 for December 2026 to February 2027.
[Gizmodo] Forecasting its effects may be complicated by climate change and because neither scientists nor climate models have seen an event of this magnitude before.
quote_evidence: With the strongest El Niño on record still intensifying, this climate phenomenon is bound to have a major influence over winter weather across the United States.

In fact, forecasting the effects of the 2026-2027 El Niño may be complicated by climate change and the fact that neither scientists nor climate models have ever seen an event of this magnitude before.
why_it_matters_hint: A record El Nino will shape weather for many people, so better forecasting tools matter.
notes: FT page returned only an error text (HTTP 403). No other outlet carries the FT piece; the El Nino context is from Gizmodo. What the FT says about AI is unknown beyond its headline question. Desk-built entry, source AI News Desk. Score lowered 1 because the AI angle is unverified.
